name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive blocks like headers and nav bars, cutting navigation time from seconds to milliseconds. The trade-off is one extra DOM node per page, which adds negligible weight but guarantees universal access for anyone who can’t use a mouse.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link entirely if it’s hidden until focused—it becomes visual noise, not a tool. A better alternative is an always-visible skip link styled to match the page’s color scheme, so it’s discoverable without sacrificing contrast. Settle it with user testing: track if keyboard users can find and use it within 3 seconds in a live prototype.
